Orbit Explore // Project Architecture & Mission Summary

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer & Deep Space Operations Platform

1. Executive Summary

Orbit Explore is a next-generation, high-performance web platform designed to simulate deep space astronaut training, mission control operations, and planetary exploration. Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the application merges real NASA astrophysics data with interactive 3D solar system visualizations, flight simulators, emergency decision-making scenarios, and astronaut training modules.

The project features a sci-fi "obsidian and neon mint" (#4EFA94) aesthetic, backed by a Node.js REST API with SQLite telemetry persistence and a React 19 / Three.js frontend.

Frontend Architecture

Framework & Build: React 19, Vite 8, ES Modules.

Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with custom HUD typography (Orbitron, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono).

3D Graphics & Visuals: Three.js & @react-three/fiber for celestial bodies and particle starfields; pure SVG vector art for zero-blur, infinite-DPI HUD visuals.

Animation Engine: Framer Motion 14 with GPU-composited transitions, layout springs, and entrance sequencing.

State Management: Zustand (uiStore.js) managing audio FX toggles, event modals, mobile drawer state, and global boot/intro sequencing.

Backend Architecture

Server: Express 4 running on Node.js 20+ with native ES Modules.

Database: SQLite via better-sqlite3 with automated schema initialization for astronaut progress and scores.

Validation & Security: Zod runtime schema validation, Helmet HTTP headers, CORS whitelisting, and IP-based rate limiting.

API Testing: Native Node test runner (node --test) covering 13 automated REST integration test suites.

1. Entrance Sequencer & UI/UX Pipeline

2.0-Second Boot Loader: On initial load or refresh, a full-screen diagnostic screen displays orbital calibration rings, glowing neon core, and sequenced telemetry messages (INITIALIZING KERNEL → SYNCHRONIZING RELAY 8.4 GHz → ALL SYSTEMS NOMINAL).

Shutter Reveal: Smooth vertical curtain slide-up (y: -100%) revealing the viewport.

Escort Tow Rocket: A vector sci-fi rocket flies across from left to right pulling the floating navbar dock into position, then hyper-accelerates away into deep space without remaining parked.

Single Crisp Page Entry: Page content transitions into view via a unified fade and float animation (opacity: 0 -> 1, y: 20 -> 0) without duplicate animations or unmount blurs.

Auto-Scroll Reset (ScrollToTop): Custom route listener resetting scroll coordinates to (0, 0) on every navigation event while supporting smooth anchor jumps.

2. Flight Deck (Home Page — /)

Mission Protocol Hero: NASA Artemis // Orbit Explore Deep Space Initiative banner.

Telemetry Metrics Bar: Key status metrics (Celestial Bodies, Life Support Closed-Loop, Telemetry Refresh 120 FPS, Phase IV Protocol).

Core Subsystem Cards: Life Support (ECLSS), 3D Celestial Physics, Command Crisis Response, and Autonomous Telemetry.

Expedition Outposts: Interactive target dossiers for Luna Base Alpha (Shackleton Crater), Mars Ares Epsilon Station (Valles Marineris), and Europa Cryo-Drill Outpost.

3. Science & Study Deck (/study)

Holographic Astronaut Spacewalker (EVA Visual): Infinite-DPI vector artwork of an astronaut in deep space with Earth reflections in the visor, glowing #4EFA94 suit indicators, live vitals (72 BPM, PRIMARY O₂: 98.4%, SUIT PRESS: 4.3 PSI), and animated umbilical tether.

3D Solar System Mechanics: Interactive planetary bodies with orbital velocities, surface gravity, radiation indices, and atmospheric densities.

NASA Mission Data Feed: Integration with NASA APOD and planetary data caches.

4. Interactive Flight Activities (/activities)

Physical Space Fitness: Simulating microgravity exercise routines (cycle ergometer, resistive exercise device).

ISS Daily Life & Habitability: Water recycling distillation, meal rehydration, and sleeping pod protocols.

Zero-G Physics Lab: Fluid dynamics, inertia demonstrations, and centripetal artificial gravity tests.

Emergency Survival Decision Simulator: Hull breach alarms, solar radiation flares, and life-support emergency triage with real-time scoring and flight certification generation.

5. Space Quiz & Astronaut Games (/games or /quiz)

5 Academic Quiz Categories: Planetary Science, Spaceflight History, Rocket Propulsion, Orbital Mechanics, and Deep Space Astronomy.

Timed Challenge & Leaderboard: Countdown quiz engine with instant score calculation and local ranking.

Arcade Mini-Games: Lunar lander descent vectoring, meteoroid hull defense, and docking alignment simulations.

4. Key Endpoints & API Reference

Method Endpoint Description

GET / API Root Metadata & Active Service Directory

GET /api/health Service uptime, database connectivity, and timestamp

GET /api/nasa-data Curated NASA space science educational dataset with cache fallback

GET /api/nasa-data/mars-weather Latest Mars atmospheric telemetry (Curiosity / InSight feeds)

GET /api/activities Complete catalog of astronaut training activities

GET /api/activities/:id Full bundle, steps, and rubric for an activity

POST /api/activities/:id/submit Validates answers, calculates score, and issues mission certification

GET /api/quiz-games/categories Returns all 5 quiz categories and questions

GET /api/quiz-games/mini-games Returns configuration for 5 astronaut arcade mini-games

POST /api/quiz-games/daily-challenge Evaluates daily challenge submissions

POST /api/quiz-games/competition Grades timed competitive space quiz

5. Quality & Performance Verification

Production Build: Zero compilation warnings or errors via Vite 8 (npm --prefix frontend run build).

Integration Tests: 13/13 passing suites via Node's native test runner (npm --prefix backend test).

Zero Raster Blur: Heavy low-res raster images replaced with ultra-lightweight, hardware-accelerated vector SVG graphics.

Git Cleanliness: All changes staged, committed, and synchronized with origin/main on GitHub.
